intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a reservation. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival day, as the market is lively and walkable from central hotels.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Culture Dive
experiences.description: Spend a day in Akihabara exploring multi-story electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, anime stores, and robot cafes. This neighborhood is the global epicenter of tech and otaku culture. Visit Yodobashi Camera, Super Potato retro games, and end with a themed cafe experience. Easily accessible by JR Yamanote Line.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, in the historic Asakusa district. Stroll Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional crafts and snacks, explore the Asakusa Shrine, and enjoy rickshaw rides through old Edo-style streets. This area is rich in traditional Japanese culture and is close to several well-located hotels.

experiences.name: Shibuya & Harajuku Street Food and Pop Culture Experience
experiences.description: Start at Harajuku's Takeshita Street for crepes and quirky fashion culture, then walk to Omotesando for upscale Japanese dining. End the day at Shibuya Crossing and explore Nonbei Yokocho (Whiskey Alley) for izakaya dining and local craft drinks. This hub covers food, youth culture, and modern Tokyo in one walkable route.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned TeamLab Borderless digital art experience, a perfect fusion of technology and Japanese aesthetics. The museum features interactive, borderless rooms of light and sound that blend art with innovation. Book tickets in advance. The new Azabudai Hills venue is centrally located and easy to reach from most Tokyo hotels.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit from airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Narita Express or Limousine Bus to central Tokyo. Check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens — free entry, stunning traditional landscape, perfect for shaking off jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Jimbocho, Chiyoda's famous book-town neighborhood. Explore the secondhand bookshops and quirky storefronts. Head to Kanda Myojin Shrine for a peaceful evening atmosphere and to soak in local culture.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a convenience store bento (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the airport — under ¥600.
meals.lunch: Pick up an onigiri and green tea from a convenience store near the hotel for a quick, affordable first meal in Tokyo — around ¥400.
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba — a legendary, affordable soba noodle restaurant near Akihabara. A bowl of classic zaru soba costs around ¥900–¥1,200. Queue may be short on a weeknight.

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, buses, and even convenience stores. Download Google Maps offline for Tokyo. April is cherry blossom season so expect some crowds and beautiful scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Palace East Gardens when they open at 9:00 AM — completely free. Walk the outer moat path lined with cherry blossoms (or late blooms in mid-April). Photograph Nijubashi Bridge and the moat reflections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short metro ride to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan. Browse retro game shops, anime merchandise, and cutting-edge gadget stalls. Many shops have free-to-browse floors with fascinating tech culture displays.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for the evening. Visit a maid café for the cultural experience — budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink and the entrance fee. Walk the illuminated main street at night, which is a spectacle in itself.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and canned coffee for around ¥500.
meals.lunch: Akihabara has excellent ramen options. Try Ichiran Ramen on the main strip — a solo-booth ramen experience for around ¥1,000. Great for solo travelers.
meals.dinner: Curry House CoCo Ichibanya near Akihabara — customizable Japanese curry rice from ¥700. A filling, beloved local chain.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara's tech culture is best experienced on foot. Many multi-story buildings hide specialty floors — look for elevator directories. Free Wi-Fi is available in most major electronics stores.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Ueno Park, a short metro ride from Chiyoda. The park is free to enter and is one of Tokyo's most beloved public spaces. Visit Ueno Toshogu Shrine (free), stroll the cherry blossom promenade, and enjoy the pond with lotus flowers and rowing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest museum with an incredible collection of samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient artifacts. Entry is ¥1,000 for adults. Spend 2–3 hours here. Afterward, browse Ameyoko Market — a bustling open-air market street near Ueno Station with cheap snacks, street food, and goods.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Yanaka Ginza, a preserved old-Tokyo shopping street that feels like stepping back in time. Browse local craft shops, try street snacks, and enjoy the nostalgic shitamachi (old town) atmosphere. Very budget-friendly with free street wandering.

meals.breakfast: Grab a morning set at a Doutor Coffee near the hotel — coffee and toast set for around ¥400–¥500.
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — try taiyaki (fish-shaped cake, ¥150), grilled skewers (¥200–¥400 each), or a fresh sashimi bowl from one of the market stalls for around ¥800.
meals.dinner: Yanaka Ginza has a small izakaya called Yanaka Beer Hall — try set meals with local beer for around ¥1,500. Alternatively, a nearby tonkatsu (pork cutlet) restaurant offers filling meals from ¥900.

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is especially beautiful in April. Arrive at the Tokyo National Museum early on weekdays to avoid school groups. Yanaka is one of Tokyo's best-preserved neighborhoods — great for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Asakusa — Tokyo's most iconic traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest temple, free to enter. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs and snacks. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to beat the weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the streets around Asakusa — Hoppy Street for local bar culture, Kappabashi Kitchenware Town (the wholesale kitchen supply district with famous plastic food displays — free to browse). Cross the Azuma Bridge for a view of the Asahi Beer Hall and Tokyo Skytree.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tokyo Skytree for the exterior view from the ground (free) and the vibrant Solamachi shopping complex at the base. The area is beautifully lit at night. If budget allows, the Tembo Deck observation floor is ¥2,100 — optional but spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a local kissaten (old-style coffee shop) near Senso-ji for a morning coffee and toast set — ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Nakamise Street snacks — ningyo-yaki (¥500 for a bag), melonpan (¥200), and amazake (sweet rice drink, ¥300). Eat as you walk.
meals.dinner: Asakusa Gyukatsu — a popular restaurant serving breaded beef cutlet with DIY grilling stones. Meals from ¥1,500. Expect a short queue on weekends but it moves fast.

day_by_day.notes: Weekends at Senso-ji are very crowded — go before 9 AM for best experience. Kappabashi is mostly closed on Sundays so Saturday is ideal. The Solamachi complex at Skytree base has great food court options for budget dining.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — take the metro to Harajuku Station. Walk through Takeshita Street, the colorful hub of youth fashion and pop culture. Browse quirky fashion boutiques, crepe stands, and candy shops. Free to walk and explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Free entry. The forested path is a peaceful contrast to the busy streets. Afterward, stroll down Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's elegant tree-lined boulevard with high-end shops and interesting architecture (window shopping is free!).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — just a short walk or one metro stop from Harajuku. Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at rush hour (most intense around 6–8 PM). Visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Sky (¥2,000) or opt for the free view from the Starbucks on the 2nd floor overlooking the crossing.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or a local bakery near Harajuku Station — melon bread and coffee for ¥400.
meals.lunch: Takeshita Street crepes — Marion Crepes is a Harajuku institution. A crepe costs ¥600–¥900. Add a bubble tea for ¥500.
meals.dinner: Shibuya Food Court in Shibuya Hikarie or SHIBUYA109 — wide variety of Japanese set meals from ¥800–¥1,200. Try a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Matsuya for a budget meal under ¥600.

day_by_day.notes: Harajuku is most vibrant on Sundays. Meiji Shrine inner garden (Iris Garden) has a small ¥500 entry fee but is optional. The Shibuya Scramble is best photographed from above — the free Starbucks window spot fills up fast, arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — take the metro from Chiyoda. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory (open from 9 AM on weekdays) for a panoramic 360-degree view of Tokyo from 202 meters — completely free. On clear days, you can see Mt. Fuji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Japan's most beautiful parks, entry ¥500. In mid-April, late cherry blossoms or spring flowers may still be blooming. Afterward, explore the narrow alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a tiny alley of yakitori stalls that's fascinating even in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Kabukicho, Shinjuku's entertainment district. Walk through the neon-lit streets and visit the Robot Restaurant area (exterior is free to observe). Visit a standing bar (tachinomi) in the Golden Gai area — tiny atmospheric bars where a drink costs ¥500–¥800.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku has excellent morning options — try a teishoku (Japanese set breakfast) at a local diner near the station for ¥600–¥800.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen has picnic areas — buy bento from a nearby convenience store and eat in the garden for a lovely ¥600 lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — grilled chicken skewers from ¥150–¥300 each. A satisfying dinner of 5–6 skewers with beer costs around ¥1,500–¥2,000. Atmospheric and authentic.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building North Tower observatory is free but closed on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month — check ahead. Golden Gai bars have small cover charges (¥500–¥1,000) but are a unique cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the free Yurikamome monorail scenic ride (covered by Suica, around ¥400 one way) for stunning bay views. Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum — book ahead online, tickets around ¥3,200. This is a world-famous immersive tech-art experience highly relevant to tech culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions — the life-size Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, the retro arcade at JOYPOLIS (exterior free), and the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Odaiba's malls have free entry and interesting architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via Yurikamome for sunset views over the bay. Head back to Chiyoda area and explore the Marunouchi district at night — beautifully lit office towers and a relaxed evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store — onigiri set and green tea for ¥500.
meals.lunch: Odaiba Aqua City food court — wide variety of Japanese cuisine from ¥800–¥1,200. Try a seafood bowl (kaisendon) for around ¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Back in Chiyoda, try a tonkatsu restaurant near Marunouchi — Maisen or a local equivalent offers pork cutlet set meals from ¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets sell out — book at least a week in advance online. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a sightseeing experience. Odaiba is best on weekdays to avoid large crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara again with a deeper focus on tech culture — explore the upper floors of Yodobashi Camera Multimedia Akiba (8 floors of electronics, free to browse). Visit the Akihabara Gamer building for retro gaming culture. Check out the Radio Kaikan building for specialty electronics and hobbyist components.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Science Museum (Kagaku Gijutsukan) near Kitanomaru Park in Chiyoda — entry ¥880, hands-on science and technology exhibits that align perfectly with tech culture interests. Spend 2 hours exploring interactive displays.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Jinbocho area in the evening — Tokyo's booktown comes alive with quirky cafes and small bars. Visit a jazz café (there are several in Jinbocho) for a cultural evening. Entry or drink minimum around ¥800–¥1,000.

meals.breakfast: Try a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) in Chiyoda for a morning set — thick toast, boiled egg, and coffee for ¥500.
meals.lunch: Akihabara has a great ramen street near the station — try tsukemen (dipping ramen) at a local shop for ¥900–¥1,100.
meals.dinner: Jinbocho Curry — the area is famous for curry restaurants. Try Bondy, a legendary European-style curry restaurant in Jinbocho, from ¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: The Science Museum is closed on Mondays and national holidays. Jinbocho's bookshops are open until around 7–8 PM on weekdays. The area has a wonderfully intellectual, old-Tokyo atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage site about 2 hours from Shinjuku by Tobu Railway (budget option: ¥1,360 one way on local trains). Visit the ornate Toshogu Shrine complex, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. The detailed carvings and gilded architecture are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple and Futarasan Shrine (combo ticket ¥1,300 covers most major sites). Walk the cedar-lined Omotesando Avenue leading to the shrines. If time permits, walk to Shinkyo Bridge — a beautiful vermilion lacquered bridge over the Daiya River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (last affordable trains around 6–7 PM). Arrive back in Chiyoda by 8–9 PM. Grab dinner near the hotel and rest.

meals.breakfast: Early start — convenience store onigiri and coffee before catching the train, around ¥500.
meals.lunch: Nikko has yuba (tofu skin) cuisine as a local specialty. Try a yuba teishoku set lunch at a restaurant near Toshogu for ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Back in Chiyoda, pick up a bento from a convenience store or grab gyudon at Sukiya for a quick, affordable dinner under ¥700.

day_by_day.notes: Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa Station for the most budget-friendly option (around ¥1,360 vs ¥2,620+ for Shinkansen). The Nikko Pass (¥4,520 round trip + unlimited local buses) may be worth it. Start early — aim for the 7 AM train.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market — Tokyo's famous seafood market area. The inner market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market still buzzes with activity. Browse fresh seafood stalls, street food vendors, and knife shops. Try fresh sushi or tamagoyaki for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens — a beautiful traditional garden with a tidal pond, entry ¥300. Take a short boat ride across the Sumida River to Asakusa (¥800 — a scenic budget river cruise). Revisit Asakusa with fresh eyes and explore the backstreets beyond the main tourist area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nakameguro for the evening — a trendy neighborhood with a canal lined with boutiques, cafes, and bars. Walk along the Meguro River canal, especially beautiful with illuminated cherry blossom trees in April. Browse the independent shops and grab a drink at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sashimi on rice (maguro don) from a market stall for ¥800–¥1,200. One of Tokyo's great food experiences.
meals.lunch: Asakusa area — try a tendon (tempura over rice) at Daikokuya Tempura, a historic restaurant from ¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Nakameguro has many affordable restaurants. Try a small Italian or Japanese bistro along the canal — budget around ¥1,200–¥1,500 for a set meal with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited between 7–10 AM when it's most active. The Sumida River water bus runs on a schedule — check Tokyo Cruise Ship timetables. Nakameguro is very photogenic at night in April.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood, famous for vintage fashion, live music venues, and indie culture. Browse the vintage clothing stores (many items from ¥500–¥2,000), record shops, and quirky cafes. A great window into Tokyo's alternative youth culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sangenjaya, a neighboring area with a more local, less touristy vibe. Explore the covered shopping arcade (shotengai), small izakayas, and local supermarkets. Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso) for affordable Japanese goods and snacks. This area shows authentic everyday Tokyo life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shinjuku for a final evening in the entertainment district. Visit the Kabukicho area for the neon spectacle, then head to the quieter Shinjuku-ni-chome area for a relaxed drink at a local bar. End the night at a ramen shop — the best ones are open until 2–3 AM.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa has excellent independent cafes — try a local coffee shop for a morning set (coffee + toast + egg) for ¥600.
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa curry — the area is dotted with affordable curry shops. A hearty keema curry set with salad costs around ¥900.
meals.dinner: Late-night ramen in Shinjuku — Fuunji (tsukemen specialist) or Ichiran for a solo ramen experience, around ¥900–¥1,100.

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best experienced on weekends when the vintage market stalls set up outside shops. The area around Shimokitazawa Station has been redeveloped — the new underground shopping street 'Shimokita COLLAR' is worth a look.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka Cemetery and Yanaka Ginza for a Sunday morning walk — the cemetery is one of Tokyo's most atmospheric, with old cherry trees and historic graves. The area survived WWII bombing and retains old Edo-era street layouts. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for a final tech culture deep-dive — visit Super Potato, a legendary retro gaming store with vintage consoles and games from the 1980s–2000s. Browse the Akihabara UDX building for tech exhibitions. Visit a figure painting workshop or hobby shop to see the detailed craft culture.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner experience — visit Yurakucho under the train tracks, near Chiyoda. This area has a row of yakitori restaurants built under the elevated railway. Atmospheric, affordable, and beloved by locals. End the evening with a walk along the Imperial Palace moat.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka area has a lovely old bakery called Kayaba Coffee (established 1938) — try their egg sandwich and coffee for ¥700. A Tokyo institution.
meals.lunch: Akihabara food floor — try a Japanese-style hamburger steak (hambagu) set at a local diner for ¥900.
meals.dinner: Yurakucho yakitori alley — grilled chicken skewers, beer, and sake in a smoky, atmospheric setting under the tracks. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 for a satisfying dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Kayaba Coffee in Yanaka opens at 8 AM on weekends. Super Potato in Akihabara is on the upper floors of a building — look for the sign. Yurakucho's restaurant alley is best experienced on a clear evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take one last walk around the Imperial Palace moat and Kitanomaru Park. Visit the Budokan (exterior) and reflect on the trip. Buy any last souvenirs from Nakamise Street in Asakusa or the Chiyoda area's convenience stores (Japanese snacks, Kit-Kats, and cosmetics make great gifts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — pack, check out of the hotel, and store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at Tokyo Station (¥400–¥700). Visit Tokyo Station's ramen street (Ramen Street in the First Avenue basement) for a final bowl. Browse the Gransta shopping complex inside Tokyo Station for premium Japanese food gifts (ekiben, wagashi sweets).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport — allow 2–3 hours before departure. Take the Narita Express or airport limousine bus. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast — stock up on Japanese snacks you love for the flight. A full breakfast of onigiri, salad, and coffee for ¥600.
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station Ramen Street — choose from 8 different ramen restaurants representing regional styles from across Japan. Budget ¥900–¥1,200 for a final bowl.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or airplane meal — if time permits before departure, Narita Airport Terminal 1 and 2 have affordable ramen and soba options from ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers at Tokyo Station fill up quickly — arrive early or use the hotel's luggage storage. The Gransta and Ecute shops inside Tokyo Station are excellent for last-minute food souvenirs (ekiben bento boxes are iconic). Return your Suica card at the airport for a refund of the ¥500 deposit.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City. Check in to the boutique hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen) — free entry, beautifully maintained grounds perfect for jet-lag recovery. Stroll along the moat and enjoy the cherry blossom aftermath or spring greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Marunouchi Naka-dori boulevard for a relaxed first evening. Window-shop the boutiques and admire the European-style architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a bento or onigiri from a convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) near the hotel to keep it simple on arrival day
meals.dinner: Kitte Marunouchi B1F food hall — try Marunouchi Tanaka Shoten for hearty ramen or visit one of the casual Japanese set-meal (teishoku) restaurants in the complex. Budget ¥1,200–1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to combat jet lag. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport or any JR station — essential for all transit throughout the trip. April in Tokyo is mild (15–22°C); pack a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo food-culture experience. Graze on fresh tamagoyaki (rolled egg), grilled scallops, tuna sashimi skewers, and matcha sweets from market stalls. Arrive by 9:00 AM for the best selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a stunning feudal-era garden with a tidal pond, tea pavilion, and peony garden. Then walk or short taxi to Ginza for window shopping and people-watching along Chuo-dori.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ginza's underground dining scene. Ginza Six B2 or Tokyu Plaza Ginza have excellent mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market stall grazing — budget ¥800–1,200 for a satisfying spread of small bites
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu Garden's Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse — matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) set for ¥1,000, taken overlooking the pond
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai in Ginza — a reliable, affordable sushi chain beloved by locals. Omakase-style ordering; budget ¥2,000–3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest 8–11 AM on weekdays. Hamarikyu is a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking today.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan for the latest gadgets, components, and retro tech. Great for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara exploring the gaming arcades (try Taito Station or SEGA), anime merchandise shops, and the unique maid café culture. Visit the Akihabara UDX building's tech showcases. Then take the train to nearby Ueno for a late-afternoon stroll through Ueno Park.
day_by_day.evening: Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) market street near Ueno Station — a vibrant, old-school outdoor market with street food, discount shops, and a lively local atmosphere. Great for evening snacking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) like Doutor or Komeda's Coffee for a morning set (toast, egg, coffee) — ¥500–700
meals.lunch: Akihabara has excellent value lunch spots — try Curry no Mise Akihabara for Japanese curry rice or a ramen shop in the backstreets. Budget ¥900–1,400
meals.dinner: Ameyoko market street food dinner — yakitori skewers, takoyaki, and grilled seafood from various stalls. Budget ¥1,500–2,000

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is a short 5-minute train ride from Chiyoda on the JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tohoku line. Friday afternoons get busy — arrive at Akihabara by 10 AM to beat crowds. Ameyoko is loudest and most fun on Friday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa — Tokyo's most atmospheric traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple at opening (6:00 AM gates open, but 9 AM is still manageable). Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki cakes, and sembei rice crackers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Azuma Bridge and visit the Sumida Aquarium (¥2,300) or opt for the free Edo-Tokyo Museum (check reopening status in 2027) to learn about Tokyo's history. Alternatively, take a 40-minute Sumida River cruise (¥1,040) from Asakusa to Hamarikyu.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nakameguro for an evening walk along the illuminated canal. The area transforms beautifully in the evening with trendy bars, cafés, and boutique restaurants lining the Meguro River.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a nearby kissaten — alternatively, buy fresh ningyo-yaki and green tea from Nakamise stalls as a light morning snack
meals.lunch: Sometaro in Asakusa — a beloved old-school okonomiyaki restaurant where you cook at the table. Budget ¥1,500–2,000
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal-side restaurant — try Wako for Japanese-French fusion or a cozy Italian bistro along the canal. Budget ¥2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Senso-ji will be crowded by mid-morning — arrive before 9 AM if possible. Nakameguro is about 30 minutes by train from Asakusa via the Hibiya Line. The canal walk is especially atmospheric after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku — visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in the morning (free entry, forested grounds, serene atmosphere). The Sunday morning crowd here is local worshippers, not tourists — a more authentic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for Tokyo's famous youth fashion and pop culture scene, then stroll along Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées — for high-end architecture and café culture. Visit the Omotesando Hills shopping complex designed by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing and Scramble Square — experience the world's busiest pedestrian crossing at rush hour (around 6–7 PM). Head up to the Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000, book online) for a panoramic night view of Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Harajuku's famous Marion Crêpes on Takeshita Street for a sweet start — ¥600–800
meals.lunch: Gyukatsu Motomura near Omotesando — crispy beef cutlet served with a personal grill, a Tokyo specialty. Budget ¥1,500–2,000
meals.dinner: Shibuya Hikarie food floors or a yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant in Shibuya. Try Gyukaku for a mid-range yakiniku experience. Budget ¥2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Book Shibuya Sky in advance online — it sells out, especially on weekends. Meiji Jingu is a 5-minute walk from Harajuku Station. Sunday in Harajuku means Takeshita Street will be very busy by noon — visit by 10:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for scenic bay views. Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (digital art museum — book tickets in advance, ¥3,200–4,500). A world-class tech-meets-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Odaiba: the giant Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free), Venus Fort outlet mall, and the beachside promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland and visit Shimbashi — a working-class salaryman district with excellent yakitori alleyways (SL Plaza area). Authentic, unpretentious, and very local.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel (onigiri + miso soup cup) or hotel café — ¥400–700
meals.lunch: Decks Tokyo Beach mall food court in Odaiba — try the Takoyaki Museum or Hong Kong Street food-themed floor for casual Asian street food. Budget ¥1,200–1,800
meals.dinner: Shimbashi yakitori alley — order skewers of chicken, vegetables, and offal with cold draft beer at a standing or seated counter bar. Budget ¥2,000–3,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets MUST be booked in advance online — they sell out weeks ahead. Check which venue (Planets or Borderless) is operating in 2027 as venues have shifted locations. The Yurikamome monorail pass (¥820 round trip) is the most scenic way to reach Odaiba.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — depart from Asakusa Station on the Tobu Nikko Line (about 2 hours, ¥1,360 one way or buy the Tobu Nikko Pass for ¥4,780 round trip with local bus access). Visit the UNESCO-listed Toshogu Shrine — one of Japan's most ornate and lavishly decorated shrine complexes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the sacred Shinkyo Bridge. Walk the cedar-lined avenues. If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls (¥550 for the elevator) — a stunning 97-meter waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (aim for a 5–6 PM train). Relax at the hotel or enjoy a quiet dinner near Chiyoda.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — or grab a convenience store bento for the train
meals.lunch: Nikko Kanaya Hotel's casual restaurant or Gyoshintei restaurant near the shrines for Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty. Budget ¥1,800–2,500
meals.dinner: Quiet dinner near Chiyoda — try a neighborhood soba restaurant for simple, restorative buckwheat noodles. Budget ¥1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. The Tobu Nikko Pass is excellent value and includes round-trip train and unlimited local buses. Start early (depart by 8 AM) to maximize time at the shrines. April weather in Nikko can be cooler than Tokyo — bring an extra layer.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku — start at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:30 AM) for a sweeping 360° view of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Then walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500) — one of Tokyo's finest parks, perfect in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's tech and electronics scene at Yodobashi Camera Multimedia Shinjuku (8 floors of electronics). Then wander through the narrow alleys of Golden Gai — a historic district of tiny bars — which is fascinating to explore even in daylight.
day_by_day.evening: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a tiny atmospheric alley of yakitori stalls near Shinjuku Station West Exit. Smoky, nostalgic, and quintessentially Tokyo. Follow with a walk through Kabukicho's neon-lit streets for the full sensory experience.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square basement food hall — pick up fresh pastries and coffee for a gourmet morning treat. Budget ¥700–1,000
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen park picnic — buy bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or the park's café and eat among the gardens. Budget ¥800–1,200
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — sit at a tiny counter and order skewers with beer. Intimate, local, and delicious. Budget ¥2,000–3,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen closes Mondays (open Wednesday). The Metropolitan Government Building has two towers — the South Tower is often less crowded. Golden Gai bars open in the evening (from 6 PM) — return later in the trip if you want to experience the bar scene.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka — Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhood. Explore Yanaka Ginza shopping street, traditional craft shops, and the historic Yanaka Cemetery (a beautiful, peaceful park-like space). This area survived WWII bombing and retains genuine Edo-era character.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to neighboring Nezu and Sendagi. Visit Nezu Shrine — a smaller, less touristy alternative to Fushimi Inari with tunnel gates and a serene pond. Then head to the Bunkyo area to visit Koishikawa Korakuen Garden (¥300) — one of Tokyo's oldest and most beautiful landscape gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Akihabara for a deeper dive — visit the Akihabara Gamers store, Super Potato (retro gaming), and if curious, experience a maid café (entry + one drink typically ¥1,000–1,500).

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza morning stalls — freshly fried menchi-katsu (meat croquettes), taiyaki fish-shaped cakes, and coffee from local shops. Budget ¥600–900
meals.lunch: Kayaba Coffee in Yanaka — a lovingly restored 1938 kissaten serving egg salad sandwiches and coffee. A Tokyo institution. Budget ¥800–1,200
meals.dinner: Akihabara ramen — try Fuunji or a local tonkotsu ramen shop in the backstreets. Budget ¥900–1,400

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The area is quiet and residential; speak softly and be respectful of locals. Nezu Shrine is a 10-minute walk from Yanaka Ginza. Koishikawa Korakuen is near Iidabashi Station on the Toei Oedo Line.

day_by_day.morning: Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower, featuring cutting-edge contemporary art with panoramic city views included. Then explore the National Art Center Tokyo nearby (free admission to building, exhibitions vary) — one of Japan's largest art spaces with stunning wave-glass architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Azabu-Juban — an upscale, international neighborhood with a village-like feel. Browse boutique shops and international food stores. Then head to Minato City's waterfront for views of Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge from the Shibaura area.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi Midtown and Roppongi Hills evening atmosphere — the outdoor plazas are beautifully lit. Friday evening in Roppongi is lively; enjoy dinner and the cosmopolitan atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — this is a slightly later start day, so take it easy
meals.lunch: Azabu-Juban's local lunch spots — try a Japanese-Italian trattoria or a tonkatsu restaurant in the area. Budget ¥1,500–2,000
meals.dinner: Roppongi Hills dining — try Gonpachi Nishiazabu (the 'Kill Bill restaurant') for izakaya-style Japanese food in a dramatic multi-story setting. Budget ¥3,000–4,500

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open until 10 PM on Fridays — ideal for evening visits too. Roppongi is about 20 minutes from Chiyoda on the Hibiya or Toei Oedo Line. Friday night in Roppongi is busy and international — a different energy from other Tokyo neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (about 1 hour, ¥940 one way). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300) — a 13-meter bronze Amida Buddha dating from 1252. Then explore Hasedera Temple (¥400) with its hilltop garden and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forests connecting several smaller shrines. Alternatively, visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important shrine — and browse the Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Spend the evening in the lively Koenji or Shimokitazawa neighborhoods for a local, bohemian Tokyo experience — record shops, vintage clothing, and live music venues.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departure from Tokyo Station
meals.lunch: Kamakura's Komachi-dori street food — try shirasudon (whitebait rice bowl) at a local restaurant, a Kamakura specialty. Budget ¥1,500–2,000
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — try a cozy curry restaurant (the area is famous for its curry shops) or a small izakaya. Budget ¥1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is very popular on weekends — depart Tokyo by 8:30 AM to beat the crowds. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line if you have one. Shimokitazawa is about 25 minutes from Shibuya on the Keio Inokashira Line — a great contrast to the touristy day.

day_by_day.morning: Kagurazaka — a charming Franco-Japanese neighborhood in the heart of Tokyo. Explore the narrow stone-paved alleyways (yokocho) lined with traditional restaurants, French bistros, and geisha houses. Visit Zenkokuji Temple (Bishamonten) and browse the artisan shops along the main street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Iidabashi and Jimbocho area — Jimbocho is Tokyo's famous book town with hundreds of secondhand bookshops, antique print stores, and specialty booksellers. A fascinating cultural and intellectual hub. Then walk to the nearby Nippon Budokan arena area for the exterior and Chidorigafuchi moat.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening — return to a favorite neighborhood for a special farewell dinner. Consider the Marunouchi or Ginza area, close to the hotel, for a slightly elevated dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Kagurazaka French bakery — the neighborhood has excellent French-Japanese fusion bakeries. Try Le Bretagne or a local boulangerie for croissants and café au lait. Budget ¥700–1,000
meals.lunch: Kagurazaka kaiseki or Japanese set lunch — many traditional restaurants offer affordable lunch sets. Try Ishikawa area restaurants for a refined but reasonably priced teishoku. Budget ¥2,000–3,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Tokyo specialty restaurant — try Tempura Tsunahachi in Shinjuku or a high-quality sushi counter for a memorable last dinner. Budget ¥4,000–6,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kagurazaka is best explored on foot — the hidden alleys are easy to miss. Sunday in Jimbocho means some shops may have limited hours — most open by 11 AM. This is a good day to buy last-minute gifts and souvenirs in Kagurazaka's craft shops.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take a peaceful early walk through the Imperial Palace East Gardens one last time, or sit in Hibiya Park (steps from Chiyoda) with a coffee and reflect on the trip. Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Marunouchi Building or Kitte Marunouchi's gift shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel (standard checkout 11 AM — arrange luggage storage if needed). Head to Tokyo Station early for airport departure. Take the Narita Express (NEX) or Limousine Bus to the airport. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final Tokyo breakfast — a proper Japanese morning set at a nearby kissaten: toast, soft-boiled egg, salad, and coffee. Budget ¥600–900
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station's Gransta underground food hall — an incredible selection of ekiben (station bento boxes) and Japanese sweets. Buy a beautiful bento for the journey. Budget ¥1,200–2,000
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Narita Express (NEX) takes about 60–90 minutes from Tokyo Station to Narita Airport; Haneda is closer (30–45 minutes). Confirm which airport your return flight departs from. Store large luggage at the hotel or use a coin locker at Tokyo Station for the morning. Buy omiyage (souvenir sweets) at Kitte Marunouchi — Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito, and Yoku Moku are popular choices.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a reservation. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival day, as the market is lively and walkable from central hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at Narita/Haneda at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer (pre-booked limousine or Blacklane car) to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen) — a 15-minute stroll from most Chiyoda hotels. Stroll the manicured grounds, admire the stone walls and moat, and shake off jet lag in one of Tokyo's most serene green spaces. Visit the nearby Nijubashi Bridge for iconic views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in the Marunouchi or Ginza district — both within easy reach of Chiyoda. Recommended: Kanda (3 Michelin stars, intimate counter dining, exquisite seasonal Japanese cuisine). Early night recommended to begin adjusting to local time.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport lounge or grab a premium bento box at Narita/Haneda before transfer
meals.dinner: Kaiseki omakase at Kanda or comparable Michelin 3-star establishment in Ginza/Marunouchi — expect ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance given the 13:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag from a long-haul flight can be significant. Pack a portable SIM or pocket Wi-Fi to pick up at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Begin the morning at the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market (a short taxi or subway ride from Chiyoda). Sample fresh nigiri sushi, golden tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and artisan street snacks from the market's top vendors. Pair with premium green tea from a specialist tea stall. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM for the freshest selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district. Visit the flagship Itoya stationery store (9 floors of Japanese design), browse luxury boutiques on Chuo-dori, and step into the Ginza Six mall's rooftop garden. Visit the Hermès Maison Ginza building, designed by Renzo Piano, for its in-house art gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) — the world-renowned sushi counter made famous by 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi.' Reservations must be made months in advance through your hotel concierge. If unavailable, alternative is Sushi Saito or Harutaka — all offering elite omakase experiences.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi and tamagoyaki at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls (Yamachō, Tamagoya Shōroku)
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Kondo (Ginza) — one of Tokyo's finest tempura restaurants, Michelin-starred
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sukiyabashi Jiro or equivalent — ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest before 10:00 AM — arrive early. Jiro Honten requires reservations far in advance; ask your hotel concierge to assist. Ginza is walkable and compact — comfortable shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: TeamLab Planets or TeamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills) — Immerse yourself in Tokyo's world-famous digital art installations. TeamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills is a cutting-edge tech-meets-art experience spanning thousands of square meters of interactive, ever-changing digital environments. Book premium timed entry in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Odaiba Tech & Innovation District — Take the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for futuristic city views. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), home to ASIMO robots, life-sized Earth displays, and exhibits on AI, space, and future technologies. Explore DiverCity Tokyo for the giant Gundam statue.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Odaiba at a waterfront restaurant with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Recommended: Tableaux (French-Japanese fusion in a dramatic setting) or return to Roppongi for dinner at Nobu Tokyo — celebrity chef Nobu Matsuhisa's flagship Japanese-Peruvian fusion restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at your Chiyoda boutique stay — request a full Japanese-style breakfast (gohan, miso shiru, grilled fish, pickles)
meals.lunch: Café lunch inside TeamLab or a ramen experience at a premium ramen shop near Azabudai Hills
meals.dinner: Nobu Tokyo (Roppongi) or waterfront fine dining in Odaiba — ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before your trip. Wear comfortable, dark clothing for TeamLab Planets (you may walk through water installations). Odaiba is best visited on a clear day for skyline views.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa Cultural Deep Dive — Visit Senso-ji Temple at dawn or early morning before crowds arrive. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, wagashi (Japanese sweets), and artisan goods. Explore the atmospheric backstreets of Yanaka nearby for a glimpse of old Shitamachi Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sumida River Yakatabune (Traditional Boat Cruise) — Board a private or premium yakatabune (traditional Japanese houseboat) for a scenic cruise along the Sumida River. Glide past Asakusa, Ryogoku, and toward Tokyo Bay with views of the Tokyo Skytree. Arrange through your hotel for a private charter with onboard seasonal cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree Observation Deck at dusk — Ascend to the Tembo Galleria (450m) for panoramic views of the city as the lights come on. Pre-book premium tickets to skip queues. Dinner afterward at a Skytree Tower restaurant or head to nearby Ryogoku for a chanko nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot) experience at a historic chanko restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a kissaten (old-school coffee shop) near Asakusa — try Pelican Café or Daikokuya area
meals.lunch: Onboard the yakatabune — seasonal bento and sake pairing, or a premium soba lunch at Kanda Yabu Soba (historic, near Akihabara)
meals.dinner: Chanko nabe at Yoshiba (Ryogoku) — a legendary sumo stable restaurant — ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most magical at 6:00–7:00 AM before tourist crowds. Private yakatabune charters can be arranged through luxury travel agencies or your hotel concierge — book 1–2 weeks in advance. April may offer cherry blossom views along the Sumida River if late bloom persists.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion — Spend the morning in Tokyo's legendary electronics and tech district. Visit Yodobashi Camera (the world's largest electronics retail complex), explore multi-floor retro game shops, anime figure stores, and cutting-edge gadget boutiques. Visit the Radio Kaikan building for rare electronics and collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Akihabara to Harajuku Transition — Travel to Harajuku to explore Omotesando, Tokyo's most architecturally stunning boulevard. Visit the Prada, Louis Vuitton, and Comme des Garçons flagship stores — each a work of architecture. Explore the Nezu Museum for exquisite Japanese antiquities and a stunning bamboo garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omotesando/Aoyama — one of Tokyo's most sophisticated dining neighborhoods. Recommended: L'Effervescence (2 Michelin stars, innovative French-Japanese cuisine using seasonal Japanese ingredients) or Florilège (2 Michelin stars, open kitchen, outstanding contemporary French-Japanese tasting menu).

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and croissant at a specialty café near Chiyoda — try % Arabica or Sarutahiko Coffee
meals.lunch: Ramen at Fuunji (Shinjuku) or a premium tonkatsu lunch at Maisen (Omotesando) — iconic pork cutlet in a converted bathhouse
meals.dinner: L'Effervescence or Florilège tasting menu — ¥25,000–¥45,000 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best on weekday mornings to avoid weekend crowds. Nezu Museum requires a short walk from Omotesando station — the garden café is a hidden gem. Book dinner reservations at L'Effervescence or Florilège months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Morning Exploration — Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for free panoramic views from the 45th floor observation deck (opens 9:30 AM). Stroll through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Japan's finest — particularly beautiful in April with late cherry blossoms or early spring flowers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinjuku Tech & Pop Culture — Explore Kakaku.com's Bic Camera flagship and the Yodobashi Akiba multi-floor electronics complex. Visit the Samurai Museum in Shinjuku for an intimate guided tour of authentic samurai armor, swords, and cultural history — with optional hands-on experiences. Explore the narrow alleys of Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Shinjuku's Kabukicho or Nishi-Shinjuku premium dining scene. Recommended: New York Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo (52nd floor, panoramic views, featured in 'Lost in Translation') — outstanding steaks and an exceptional wine list. Alternatively, try Kozue (40th floor, Park Hyatt) for refined kaiseki with city views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium morning set at a Shinjuku hotel café
meals.lunch: Soba at Honmura An (Roppongi) or a premium bento at Isetan Shinjuku department store's basement food hall (depachika)
meals.dinner: New York Grill or Kozue at Park Hyatt Tokyo — ¥25,000–¥45,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entry fee but is well worth it. The Park Hyatt Tokyo New York Grill requires reservations — book through your hotel concierge. Explore the Isetan Shinjuku depachika (basement food hall) for exceptional Japanese food shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko — Arrange a private car or take the Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa (approx. 2 hours). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — a breathtaking display of Edo-period craftsmanship, ornate carvings, and gilded architecture set in ancient cedar forests. Arrive early to beat tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — Visit Rinno-ji Temple and the serene Shinkyo (Sacred Bridge) over the Daiya River. Walk through the Kanmangafuchi Abyss, a mystical riverside path lined with moss-covered Jizo statues. If time permits, visit Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by private transfer or express train. Relaxed dinner near Chiyoda — try Tohoku Sanchoku Inshokuten for exceptional regional Japanese cuisine, or a quiet dinner at a high-end teppanyaki restaurant. Early evening return recommended.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a traditional Nikko restaurant — a local specialty. Recommended: Gyoshintei, a beautiful garden restaurant serving shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine)
meals.dinner: Premium teppanyaki at Ukai-tei (Omotesando) or a relaxed kaiseki dinner near Chiyoda — ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nikko requires an early start — aim to leave by 7:00–8:00 AM. A private car hire makes the experience more flexible and comfortable. Tosho-gu can be crowded midday — explore outer areas first. Comfortable walking shoes essential for Nikko's hilly terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Roppongi Art Triangle — Begin at the Mori Art Museum (Roppongi Hills, 53rd floor) for world-class contemporary art with extraordinary city views. Walk to the National Art Center Tokyo — Japan's largest exhibition space — for rotating major exhibitions. Complete the triangle at the Suntory Museum of Art in Tokyo Midtown.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo Midtown & Design Hub — Explore the curated shops and galleries at Tokyo Midtown, a premium mixed-use complex featuring the 21_21 Design Sight (founded by Issey Miyake and Tadao Ando) — a must-visit for design and tech culture enthusiasts. Browse the Hinoki Public Relations shop for exceptional Japanese craft goods.
day_by_day.evening: Private sake tasting and Japanese whisky experience — arrange through your hotel for a guided premium tasting session at a specialist sake bar or whisky bar in Roppongi or Ginza. Recommended venues: The SG Club (Shibuya) or Bar High Five (Ginza) — among the world's best cocktail bars with exceptional Japanese whisky selections. Light dinner pairing included.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at a serene hotel restaurant or nearby kissaten
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mori Art Museum café or a premium bento from Roppongi Hills' artisan food shops
meals.dinner: Omakase Japanese whisky/sake pairing dinner at a specialist bar — ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person for premium drinks and small plates

day_by_day.notes: Book the 21_21 Design Sight visit in advance as exhibitions change seasonally. Bar High Five in Ginza is a legendary cocktail bar — reservations essential. The Mori Art Museum stay-late option (open until 22:00 on most days) allows evening city views.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka & Nezu Neighborhood Walk — Explore one of Tokyo's most beautifully preserved historic neighborhoods. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (peaceful and full of character), browse the Yanaka Ginza shopping street for artisan crafts, ceramics, and local snacks. Visit the Yanaka neighborhood's independent galleries and century-old temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Cultural Corridor — Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing over 110,000 items of Japanese art, samurai artifacts, Buddhist sculptures, and ancient ceramics. Explore the Heiseikan wing for special exhibitions. Walk through Ueno Park, still beautiful in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the upscale Kagurazaka neighborhood — known as 'Little Paris' for its French-Japanese culinary scene and atmospheric stone-paved alleys. Recommended: Ishikawa (3 Michelin stars, refined kaiseki in an intimate setting) or La Tourelle (elegant French cuisine in a historic building). Explore the hidden geisha district laneways after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Artisan bakery breakfast in Yanaka — try Kayaba Coffee (a beautifully preserved 1938 kissaten) for morning coffee and toast
meals.lunch: Ueno's Ameya-Yokocho market street for casual street food, or a premium bento from the Tokyo National Museum restaurant
meals.dinner: Ishikawa (Kagurazaka) kaiseki — ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot with no rush — allow 2–3 hours. Tokyo National Museum requires advance ticket booking for special exhibitions. Kagurazaka's hidden alleys (yokocho) are magical at night — explore after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Tech & Culture Morning — Visit the Shibuya Scramble Square observation deck (SHIBUYA SKY, 230m) for spectacular 360-degree views. Explore the Shibuya Stream and Hikarie complexes — cutting-edge mixed-use developments representing Tokyo's urban innovation. Visit Shibuya's famous Scramble Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku & Daikanyama — Walk from Harajuku through Omotesando to the chic Daikanyama neighborhood. Visit the iconic Tsutaya Books (Daikanyama T-Site) — a beautifully designed bookstore and cultural complex set in a forest garden. Explore Nakameguro's canal-lined streets, boutique shops, and specialty coffee roasters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Nakameguro or Ebisu — one of Tokyo's most fashionable dining neighborhoods. Recommended: Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon (Yebisu Garden Place, Ebisu) — a stunning French gastronomy experience in a château setting, with multiple Michelin stars. One of the most luxurious dining experiences in all of Japan.

meals.breakfast: Specialty coffee and pastry at a Shibuya café — try Fuglen Tokyo (Norwegian specialty coffee roaster) or Blue Bottle Coffee Shibuya
meals.lunch: Wagyu beef lunch at Nakameguro's Yakiniku Jumbo Hanare or a premium sushi lunch at a Daikanyama counter
meals.dinner: Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon (Ebisu) — ¥40,000–¥70,000 per person with wine pairing. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: SHIBUYA SKY tickets should be booked online in advance. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2:00 AM) — a unique late-night cultural experience. Joël Robuchon Ebisu is one of Tokyo's most formal dining experiences — smart dress code required.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Hakone — Arrange a private luxury transfer or take the Romancecar Limited Express from Shinjuku (90 minutes). Visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum — Japan's first open-air art museum, with sculptures by Picasso, Rodin, and Henry Moore set against mountain scenery. On clear days, enjoy views of Mt. Fuji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hakone Cultural & Natural Wonders — Take the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani (sulfur vents, black eggs) to Lake Ashi. Enjoy a traditional wooden sightseeing cruise on Lake Ashi with views of Mt. Fuji reflected in the water. Visit Hakone Shrine, a stunning lakeside torii gate emerging from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight ryokan experience in Hakone (optional upgrade) or return to Tokyo. If staying: Check into a luxury ryokan (Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu) for kaiseki dinner, private onsen bath, and the full traditional Japanese inn experience. If returning: Dinner in Shinjuku upon arrival.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Black egg (kuro-tamago) snack at Owakudani and a lakeside lunch near Ashi — or a premium bento on the Romancecar train
meals.dinner: Multi-course kaiseki dinner at Gora Kadan ryokan (if staying overnight) — ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person including accommodation and meals. Or: Dinner in Shinjuku if returning to Tokyo.

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — morning views are clearest. The Hakone Free Pass covers most transport within Hakone and is worth purchasing. If upgrading to ryokan overnight, book Gora Kadan months in advance — it is one of Japan's most celebrated luxury ryokans.

day_by_day.morning: Return from Hakone (if overnight) or begin Tokyo's Marunouchi & Imperial Palace Circuit — Walk the elegant Marunouchi business district, Tokyo's financial and architectural showpiece. Visit the Mitsubishi Ichigokan Museum for Western art exhibitions. Walk the Imperial Palace outer gardens and the Chidorigafuchi moat — one of Tokyo's most beautiful spots in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Japanese Craft & Shopping Experience — Visit the Mitsukoshi Ginza or Isetan Shinjuku department stores for curated Japanese crafts, lacquerware, ceramics, textiles, and premium food gifts. Visit the Okura Museum of Art (adjacent to Hotel Okura) for extraordinary Japanese art in an intimate setting. Browse Coredo Muromachi in Nihonbashi for artisan Japanese goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Omakase Dinner — Reserve a final extraordinary dining experience at one of Tokyo's elite restaurants. Recommended: Sazenka (2 Michelin stars, exceptional Chinese-Japanese fusion kaiseki by chef Tomoya Kawada) or Quintessence (3 Michelin stars, French gastronomy with Japanese philosophy). Pair with a post-dinner stroll through illuminated Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast (if returning from Hakone) or a premium hotel breakfast in Tokyo
meals.lunch: Depachika exploration lunch — assemble a luxury bento from Mitsukoshi or Isetan basement food halls
meals.dinner: Quintessence or Sazenka — ¥35,000–¥60,000 per person. One of the finest meals of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Chidorigafuchi moat boat rentals are popular in cherry blossom season — arrive early. The depachika (department store basement food halls) of Mitsukoshi and Isetan are extraordinary food experiences in themselves. Final evening — take time to revisit favorite neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Final Morning in Tokyo — Sleep in and enjoy a slow, luxurious hotel breakfast. Take a final stroll through the Imperial Palace East Gardens or along the Chidorigafuchi moat. Visit a nearby specialty tea shop for premium matcha gifts — try Ippodo Tea (Marunouchi) for exceptional ceremonial-grade matcha and tea sets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-Minute Experiences & Departure Preparation — Visit Nihonbashi for final souvenir shopping at Coredo Muromachi or Takashimaya. Pick up premium Japanese food gifts: wagashi (traditional sweets), premium dashi, Japanese whisky, or artisan ceramics. Return to hotel, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow 3+ hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Enjoy the premium airport lounge (JAL Sakura Lounge, ANA Suite Lounge, or international carrier lounge) for a final taste of Japanese hospitality before boarding. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast — savor a final Japanese-style or Western breakfast at your Chiyoda boutique stay
meals.lunch: Premium sushi or ramen at a Nihonbashi restaurant before departure — try Sushi Harutaka (if available) or Nihonbashi Dashi Bar Hanare for a light, elegant farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium/first-class meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Tokyo traffic can be unpredictable, especially on weekday afternoons. Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Pre-book your airport transfer through your hotel concierge. Pack Japanese purchases carefully — liquids and food items may have customs restrictions. Consider using a takkyubin (luggage delivery) service to send heavy bags directly to the airport the day before.
